GST Late Payment Interest
Section 50 — interest on delayed tax payment

Inputs

Under Section 50 of the CGST Act, interest at 18% p.a. applies on tax paid after the due date, computed on a daily basis for the number of days the payment is delayed. Interest on wrongly availed and utilised ITC is charged at 24% p.a. — adjust the rate above if that applies to your case.

Period-wise filing calendar with mark-as-filed status

Add filing period

Standard due dates: GSTR-1 monthly filers — 11th of next month; QRMP filers — 13th of month after quarter end. GSTR-3B — 20th (monthly) or 22nd/24th (QRMP, state-dependent). Sec 234F (ITR) & Sec 47 CGST Act (GST returns)
ITRSec 234F
GST ReturnSec 47

ITR Late Filing Fee — Sec 234F

Filed on/before due date

GST Return Late Fee — Sec 47

GSTR-3B

No

ITR late fee u/s 234F: ₹5,000 if filed after the due date; reduced to ₹1,000 if total income does not exceed ₹5,00,000. No fee if return isn't otherwise required to be filed. GST late fee u/s 47: ₹50/day (₹25 CGST + ₹25 SGST) for normal returns, ₹20/day (₹10+₹10) for Nil returns, subject to per-Act caps and, for GSTR-9/9C, an overall cap linked to turnover. These are standard statutory rates — government notifications have periodically reduced/waived late fees, so cross-check the current position before relying on this for a client.

E-Way Bill Validity Calculator
Rule 138 — validity period from distance

Inputs

Normal cargo1 day / 200 km
Over-dimensional1 day / 20 km
Under Rule 138 of the CGST Rules: for normal cargo, validity is 1 day for every 200 km (or part thereof); for over-dimensional cargo, 1 day for every 20 km (or part thereof). Part of a day counts as a full day. The relevant date/time is when the e-way bill is generated, and validity can be extended by the transporter within the permitted window before/after expiry.

Structure check, checksum & PAN/state decode

Enter GSTIN

GSTIN structure: 2 digits state code + 10-char PAN + 1 entity code + 'Z' (default) + 1 checksum digit. This performs a structural and checksum check only — it does not confirm the GSTIN is actually registered/active; verify live status on the GST portal.

Input Tax Credit (ITC) Calculator
Eligible ITC after blocked credit & Rule 42 reversal

Inputs

Simplified Rule 42/43 approach: common credit (after removing blocked ITC) is apportioned to exempt supplies in the ratio of exempt turnover to total turnover, and that portion is reversed. For a precise reversal, ITC attributable exclusively to taxable/exempt supplies should be identified first — this tool assumes all remaining ITC is common credit.

Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM) Calculator
GST payable by recipient under RCM

Inputs

5%
12%
18%
28%
Intra-stateCGST + SGST
Inter-stateIGST
Under RCM, the recipient pays GST directly to the government (cannot be paid via ITC) and, if the goods/services are used for business, can then claim the same as ITC in the same return period — so it is typically cash-flow neutral. Common RCM supplies include GTA services, legal services from an advocate, services by a director, and supplies from unregistered persons in notified cases.

Composition Scheme Tax Calculator
Quarterly tax payable under Sec 10 composition levy

Inputs

Manufacturer1%
Restaurant5%
Trader1% (taxable)
Composition rates: Manufacturers/Traders — 1% (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST); Restaurants (not serving alcohol) — 5%; Other service providers under Sec 10(2A) — 6%. Composition dealers file quarterly statement CMT-08 and annual return GSTR-4, cannot collect GST from customers or claim ITC, and are eligible only up to ₹1.5 crore aggregate turnover (₹75 lakh for special category states).

Match supplier-wise ITC: portal vs your books

Add Supplier Entry

Mismatches usually arise from: supplier not filing GSTR-1, timing differences (invoice booked in a different period than reflected), or data-entry errors. ITC can generally be claimed only to the extent reflected in GSTR-2B under Sec 16(2)(aa) — investigate any "Books > Portal" line before claiming the excess.

QRMP Scheme Calculator
Monthly PMT-06 estimate under the Fixed Sum Method

Inputs

Fixed Sum (35%)
Self-Assessment
Under QRMP, GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B are filed quarterly, but tax is deposited monthly for the first two months via challan PMT-06 — either at a flat 35% of the cash tax paid in the last quarter's Q3 month (Fixed Sum Method), or the actual tax due for that month (Self-Assessment Method). No deposit is needed for a month if the ITC available fully covers the liability.

Decide POS & applicable tax head for a transaction

Inputs

Goods
Services
Yes (goods move)
No / bill-to-ship-to
General rules (Sec 10-13, IGST Act): for goods with movement, POS is the location where movement terminates; for services (default rule), POS is the recipient's location if registered, else the supplier's location. Special rules apply for immovable property, transportation, telecom, banking, and a few other categories — this tool covers the default/general rule only.

GST Refund Calculator
Refund of excess balance in electronic cash ledger

Inputs

Excess Cash Ledger Balance
Export (LUT, without payment)
Refund applications (RFD-01) must be filed within 2 years of the relevant date. Export refund formula (Rule 89(4)): Refund = (Turnover of zero-rated supply × Net ITC) ÷ Adjusted Total Turnover. Any excess cash ledger balance can simply be withdrawn via RFD-01 without further formula.

TCS under GST Calculator
TCS collectible by e-commerce operators — Sec 52

Inputs

Intra-state
Inter-state
TCS rate under Sec 52 is 1% of the net value of taxable supplies made through the e-commerce operator (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST for intra-state, or 1% IGST for inter-state). Net value = aggregate value of taxable supplies (excluding exempt) less supplies returned. TCS collected is deposited by the ECO by the 10th of the following month and reflects in the supplier's electronic cash ledger.

GSTR-9 / 9C Applicability Checker
Annual return & reconciliation statement thresholds

Inputs

Regular
Composition
GSTR-9 is optional for taxpayers with aggregate turnover up to ₹2 crore in a financial year (they may still file voluntarily), and mandatory above that. GSTR-9C (self-certified reconciliation statement) is required only for taxpayers with aggregate turnover above ₹5 crore. Composition dealers file GSTR-9A-equivalent details are captured within GSTR-4 instead of GSTR-9.

Inverted Duty Structure Refund Calculator
Refund of accumulated ITC — Rule 89(5)

Inputs

Formula under Rule 89(5): Max Refund = [(Turnover of inverted-rated supply of goods and services × Net ITC) ÷ Adjusted Total Turnover] − Tax payable on such inverted-rated supply. Net ITC here means ITC availed on inputs only during the period (input services and capital goods are excluded from this formula).

Track goods sent for job work & 1yr/3yr return deadlines

Add Job Work Entry

Inputs1 year
Capital Goods3 years
Under Sec 143, inputs sent for job work must be received back (or supplied further) within 1 year, and capital goods within 3 years, of being sent out — failing which the movement is deemed a taxable supply on the original despatch date, with tax and interest payable. Moulds, dies, jigs, fixtures, and tools sent for job work are exempt from this time limit.

E-Invoice (IRN) Applicability Checker
Is e-invoicing mandatory for this business?

Inputs

Normal taxpayer
SEZ Unit / Insurer / Bank / GTA / Exempt category
As per the latest CBIC notifications, e-invoicing (IRN generation via an IRP) is mandatory for B2B/export/credit-debit note supplies once aggregate turnover exceeds ₹5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18 onwards. SEZ Units (not SEZ Developers), insurers, banks/NBFCs, GTAs, passenger transport services, and a few other notified categories are exempt regardless of turnover. Always verify against the current CBIC notification as this threshold has been progressively lowered over time.

RCM on GTA Calculator
Reverse charge for Goods Transport Agency freight

Inputs

5% under RCMRecipient pays, no ITC to GTA
12% Forward ChargeGTA pays, ITC allowed
A GTA (issuing a consignment note) can opt, at the start of the financial year, to pay GST under forward charge at 12% (with ITC) or 5% (without ITC). If the GTA does not opt for forward charge, the specified recipient (factory, society, registered person, company, partnership firm, casual taxable person, etc.) must pay GST under RCM at 5%, without ITC to the GTA (recipient can claim ITC if otherwise eligible). GTAs exclusively supplying to unregistered/non-specified persons are exempt.

Mixed vs Composite Supply Classifier
Sec 8 — determine tax treatment of bundled supplies

Answer the following

Yes
No
Yes
No
Yes
No
Composite supply (Sec 2(30)): naturally bundled with a principal supply — taxed at the rate applicable to the principal supply (e.g. goods + transport + insurance sold together). Mixed supply (Sec 2(74)): two or more individual supplies combined for a single price, not naturally bundled — taxed at the rate of the item attracting the highest GST rate in the bundle.

GST on Advance — Real Estate Calculator
Under-construction property: GST on 2/3rd value (land deemed 1/3rd)

Inputs

Affordable Housing1%, no ITC
Other Residential/Commercial5%, no ITC
For under-construction residential/commercial projects (post-April 2019 scheme), GST applies on two-thirds of the amount charged, since one-third is deemed the value of land/undivided share and stands abated. Rates (without ITC): Affordable housing — 1% effective; Other residential/commercial — 5% effective. No GST applies once the completion certificate is issued or on the first occupation, whichever is earlier.

Nil Return Reminder
Track clients with no activity — don't miss mandatory Nil filings

Add Client on Nil-Filing Watch

Even with zero turnover, GSTR-3B and GSTR-1 must be filed for every registered GSTIN unless the registration is suspended/cancelled. Nil GSTR-3B can be filed via SMS. Missing a Nil return still attracts late fee u/s 47 (₹20/day, capped) and can eventually lead to registration cancellation for continuous default.

Interest on Delayed ITC Reversal Calculator
Sec 50(3) — interest on wrongly availed/utilised ITC

Inputs

Interest under Sec 50(3) applies at 18% p.a. where ITC has been wrongly availed and utilised (if merely availed but not utilised, no interest arises since it stays as a book credit). Interest runs from the date of utilisation of such credit to the date of reversal/payment. This calculator uses the date ITC was availed as a proxy for the utilisation date where the exact utilisation date isn't separately tracked — adjust accordingly if utilisation happened later.

Casual / NRTP Registration Calculator
Advance tax deposit for temporary registration

Inputs

A Casual Taxable Person or Non-Resident Taxable Person must deposit an advance tax equal to the estimated net tax liability for the registration period at the time of applying for registration (Sec 27). Validity is limited to 90 days from the effective date, extendable by a further 90 days on additional advance deposit. The deposit is credited to the electronic cash ledger and used to discharge the actual liability.

Depreciation — Block of Assets
Sec 32, Income Tax Act — WDV method

Block details

5%
10%
15%
40%
Under Sec 32, depreciation is computed on the WDV of the block of assets, not per-asset. Assets put to use for 180 days or more in the year get the full rate; assets used for less than 180 days get half the rate. If the block value goes to zero or negative (asset sold for more than WDV + additions), the balance is a short-term capital gain and no depreciation is allowed that year.

TDS Interest & Late Fee
Sec 201(1A) interest + Sec 234E late fee

Inputs

Late deduction1% / month
Late deposit1.5% / month
Interest under Sec 201(1A) is charged per calendar month or part thereof — 1% p.m. for late deduction (from date TDS was deductible to date actually deducted), and 1.5% p.m. for late deposit (from date deducted to date actually deposited). Sec 234E late fee for delayed TDS/TCS return filing is ₹200 per day, capped at the TDS amount.

Inventory Valuation
FIFO vs Weighted Average

Add purchase batch

Units sold / issued

FIFO assumes the oldest batches are sold first, leaving the most recent purchase cost in closing stock. Weighted Average blends all batch costs into a single rate for both COGS and closing stock.

Bad Debts & Provision
Write-off, new provision & P&L impact in one flow

Trial Balance figures

Adjustments

Further bad debts are first written off against Sundry Debtors, then the new provision is calculated on the remaining (good) debtors. The P&L charge nets the bad debts written off against the change in provision — a fall in provision is credited back to P&L rather than shown separately.

Rectification of Errors
Suspense A/c working & rectifying entries

Trial balance difference

Add an error found

One-sided errors — wrong casting/totaling, posting to the wrong side, or posting only one aspect of an entry — are the only ones that show up as a trial balance difference, so they're the only ones routed through the Suspense A/c. Errors of principle, compensating errors, and complete omissions affect a debit and a credit equally, so the trial balance still tallies and no Suspense A/c entry is needed for them.

Partner's Remuneration
Sec 40(b) — maximum allowable remuneration

Inputs

Under Sec 40(b), maximum allowable remuneration to working partners is: ₹1,50,000 or 90% of book profit (whichever is more) on the first ₹3,00,000 of book profit — or in case of a loss — plus 60% of book profit exceeding ₹3,00,000. Remuneration paid must also be authorised by the partnership deed to be allowed as a deduction.

Add month's statement

About CA Desk
Version & information

CA Desk

Version1.0
PurposeProfessional toolkit for CAs
Made byAyussh Ingulkar
CA Desk is a single-file toolkit covering GST, Income Tax, TDS, Accounting, Audit, Finance, Compliance tracking, and Client management calculators — built for quick, offline-friendly use during client work. All data you enter (favorites, client lists, checklists, fee records) is stored locally on this device and is not sent to any server.
Figures and due dates reflect standard statutory provisions at the time of writing and are provided for quick reference only — always verify against the latest Act, Rules, and government notifications before relying on them for filing or advice.
←
🔒 App Lock (PIN)
Require a PIN every time CA Desk opens
Your App Lock PIN is stored only on this device and is deliberately left out of Backup & Restore exports — so a backup file never carries your lock PIN, and restoring a backup on another device never changes or removes the PIN already set there. If you forget your PIN, use "Remove PIN" from a session where the app is already unlocked, or clear this device's app data to reset.

Backup & Restore Data
Export or import everything stored in CA Desk

Export

Downloads a single JSON file with everything stored in CA Desk on this device — every module, not just some: clients, invoices, fees, tasks, document expiries, time logs, checklists, Khata (items, sections, sales, payments, customers), Business Folders, Staff, Personal Finance, calculator history, your Profile, and preferences.

Restore

Choose a previously exported CA Desk backup file. You'll see exactly what's inside — and how it compares to what's already on this device — before anything is changed.

CA Desk stores everything locally on this device (or in Claude's artifact storage when run inside Claude), with no cloud sync — this backup file is your way of keeping a copy elsewhere or moving your data to another device/browser. Only the modules actually present in the chosen file are touched; anything else already on this device is left exactly as it is.

Presumptive Taxation
Sec 44AD (business) & Sec 44ADA (profession)

Inputs

44ADBusiness
44ADAProfession

Compare with actual profit (optional)

Sec 44AD — presumptive income is 6% of turnover received digitally/by banking channels and 8% of turnover received in cash, provided total turnover is within ₹3 crore (₹2 crore if using the old limit) — no need to maintain books or get a tax audit if you declare at least these rates. Sec 44ADA — for specified professionals, presumptive income is 50% of gross receipts, provided receipts are within ₹75 lakh (₹50 lakh under the old limit) — same audit/books exemption applies. These are simplified checks; final eligibility depends on turnover thresholds, cash-receipt proportion, and other conditions under the Act.
←
HUF Tax Calculator
Hindu Undivided Family — Old vs New Regime

Income details

Use the Section 80 Deductions Calculator below to work out the Chapter VI-A figure above if you haven't already.
Key HUF-specific point: an HUF is taxed on the same slabs as an individual under both regimes, but it is not eligible for the Section 87A rebate — that rebate applies only to resident individuals. So even where an individual's tax would be reduced to Nil (taxable income up to ₹12,00,000 under the new regime), an HUF with the same taxable income still pays tax at slab rates. HUFs also don't get any age-based higher exemption, since an HUF has no "age".
Old Regime slabs used: 0–2.5L Nil · 2.5–5L 5% · 5–10L 20% · above 10L 30%. New Regime slabs (FY 2025-26): 0–4L Nil · 4–8L 5% · 8–12L 10% · 12–16L 15% · 16–20L 20% · 20–24L 25% · above 24L 30%. Both add 4% Health & Education Cess. Chapter VI-A deductions (80C, 80D, etc.) apply only under the Old Regime; the New Regime taxable income here is taken as Gross Total Income as-is (HUFs typically have no salary/pension income, so no standard deduction is assumed — adjust manually if that applies to your case).
←

80C / 80CCC / 80CCD(1)

Capped at ₹1,50,000 combined.

80TTA / 80TTB — Savings/Deposit Interest

Below 6080TTA · Cap ₹10,000

80E — Education Loan Interest

No upper cap — full interest is deductible, for up to 8 years from when repayment starts.

80G — Donations

Enter the amount already eligible for deduction — 80G has donee-specific rates (50% or 100%) and some categories cap the deduction at 10% of adjusted gross total income, which this calculator doesn't compute for you.
These deductions apply only under the Old Tax Regime. The New Regime disallows almost all Chapter VI-A deductions (the main exceptions are the standard deduction on salary and 80CCD(2) employer NPS contribution, neither shown here). Copy the total below into the Chapter VI-A field of the HUF Calculator, Old vs New Regime Comparison, or the main Income Tax Calculator when working out Old Regime tax by hand.

Advance tax paid — cumulative by each due date (₹)

Return filing

Simplified estimator: 1% per month (or part of a month) on the shortfall for each section. 234A — for late filing, on tax payable after TDS & advance tax, from the day after the due date to filing date. 234B — if advance tax paid by 31 Mar is under 90% of assessed tax, on the shortfall from 1 April to filing/determination date. 234C — on shortfall against the 15%/45%/75%/100% cumulative installment schedule (3 months' interest for Jun/Sep/Dec shortfalls, 1 month for Mar). Actual computation has exceptions (e.g. 234C relief where shortfall is within 12%/10% of tax due, or arises from capital gains) not modelled here — verify for filing-grade accuracy.
←
Set-off & Carry Forward of Losses
Chapter VI, Sec 70–80

Income / loss by head (₹)

Simplified ordering: capital losses are netted within the capital-gains head first (STCL can offset STCG or LTCG; LTCL only offsets LTCG). House Property loss is then set off against any head (capped ₹2,00,000/year), followed by Business loss against all heads except Salary. Unabsorbed amounts carry forward: HP loss 8 years (against HP income only), Business loss 8 years (against business income only, 4 years if speculative), Capital losses 8 years (against capital gains of the same nature). Actual return-filing computation may involve additional nuances (unabsorbed depreciation, speculative business, etc.) not modelled here.
←
Salary Breakup / Form 16 Estimator
Gross salary → taxable salary income

Salary components (₹/year)

80CCD(2) employer NPS contribution is deductible under both regimes (up to 14% of Basic+DA for Central Govt employees, 10% for others — this tool doesn't cap it, so enter the eligible figure). Use the HRA and LTA exemption calculators separately for precise exempt amounts.
←
Gratuity & Leave Encashment Exemption
Sec 10(10) & 10(10AA)

Gratuity — Sec 10(10)

Covered
Not covered

Leave Encashment (on retirement) — Sec 10(10AA)

Gratuity: exemption is the least of (a) amount received, (b) ₹20,00,000, and (c) — if covered — 15/26 × last drawn salary × years of service (part-year ≥6 months rounded up); if not covered — ½ × avg. salary of last 10 months × completed years of service (no rounding). Leave encashment (non-government employees only): least of amount received, ₹25,00,000, 10 months' average salary, and the cash equivalent entered above. Fully exempt for government employees.
←
Virtual Digital Assets (Crypto) Tax
Sec 115BBH & TDS u/s 194S

Transaction details

VDA (crypto/NFT) gains are taxed flat at 30% + 4% cess, with no deduction other than cost of acquisition — no exemption limit, no set-off against any other income, and losses cannot be carried forward or set off even against other VDA gains. Buyer must deduct 1% TDS u/s 194S on the sale consideration (thresholds: ₹50,000/year for specified persons, ₹10,000/year for others).
←
Lottery / Game Winnings Tax
Sec 115BB & 115BBJ

Winnings details

Lottery/Betting/Card GamesSec 115BB
Online GamesSec 115BBJ
Winnings from lotteries, crossword puzzles, races, card games, betting/gambling (Sec 115BB) and online games (Sec 115BBJ, on net winnings for the year) are taxed flat at 30% + 4% cess — no expenses, deductions, or basic exemption limit apply, and such losses can't be set off against any other income. TDS: 30% u/s 194B (lottery, above ₹10,000) or 194BA (online games, on net winnings withdrawn).
←
TDS on Property Purchase
Sec 194-IA — Immovable property (resident seller)

Transaction details

ResidentSec 194-IA
NRISec 195
For a resident seller, buyer deducts 1% TDS on the entire consideration (not just the excess) if it's ₹50 lakh or more — below that, no TDS applies. For an NRI seller, Sec 195 applies instead: TDS is on the capital gain component at LTCG/STCG rates plus surcharge and cess (not a flat 1% on consideration), and typically needs a lower/nil-deduction certificate from the seller's AO to avoid TDS on the full sale value — this tool doesn't compute that; consult Sec 195 provisions separately.
←
TCS on Foreign Remittance
Sec 206C(1G) — Liberalised Remittance Scheme

Remittance details

FY 2025-26 thresholds (per remitter, aggregated across the year): first ₹7,00,000 is Nil for all categories except Overseas Tour Packages (5%). Beyond ₹7,00,000: Education via specified loan — 0.5%; Education (self-funded)/Medical — 5%; Overseas Tour Package — 20%; Other remittances (investments, gifts, etc.) — 20%. Rates and thresholds are revised periodically by the Finance Act — verify the current CBDT notification before relying on this for filing.
←
Gift Tax
Sec 56(2)(x) — Income from Other Sources

Gift details

From relative / on marriage / under willFully exempt
Not exempt
Cash
Movable Property
Immovable Property
Gifts from "relatives" (as defined — spouse, siblings, lineal ascendants/descendants, siblings of parents/spouse, etc.), gifts on the occasion of marriage, and property received under a will/inheritance are fully exempt regardless of value. Otherwise: cash gifts are taxable in full once aggregate gifts in the year exceed ₹50,000; movable property without consideration is taxable at FMV if it exceeds ₹50,000 (with consideration, only if FMV − consideration > ₹50,000); immovable property without consideration is taxable at Stamp Duty Value if it exceeds ₹50,000 (with consideration, only if SDV − consideration exceeds the higher of ₹50,000 or 10% of consideration).
←
Clubbing of Income
Sec 60–64

Minor child's income — Sec 64(1A)

Other common clubbing situations (Sec 60–64) — no calculator needed, add the full amount to the transferor's income: income from an asset transferred to a spouse or son's wife without adequate consideration (Sec 64(1)(iv)/(vi)); income of a spouse as remuneration from a concern in which the individual has a substantial interest (>20% voting power/profit share), unless the spouse's own technical/professional qualification justifies it (Sec 64(1)(ii)); income from assets transferred to any person for the benefit of a spouse or son's wife (Sec 64(1)(vii)/(viii)); and income from a revocable transfer of assets (Sec 61). Minor's clubbed income is added to the parent with the higher income (or, once clubbed, continues with that parent in later years unless the AO decides otherwise).
←
Agricultural Income Integration
Partial integration for rate purposes — Old Regime

Income details

Below 60Cap ₹2.5L
60–80Cap ₹3L
Above 80Cap ₹5L
Applies only if Net Agricultural Income exceeds ₹5,000 and Non-Agricultural Income exceeds the basic exemption limit — and only where the taxpayer opts for the Old Regime (the New Regime's fixed slab structure doesn't use this partial-integration mechanism in practice). Method: compute tax on (Non-agri + Agri) income at slab rates, compute tax on (Basic Exemption Limit + Agri) income at slab rates, and the difference is the tax before rebate/cess. Agricultural income itself stays exempt — this mechanism only affects the rate applied to non-agricultural income.

Depreciation Schedule — Schedule II
Companies Act, 2013 — full year-wise schedule generator

Asset details

SLMStraight-line
WDVWritten-down value
Under Schedule II to the Companies Act, 2013, depreciation is computed over the useful life prescribed in Part C (or a technically justified different life, with disclosure), with the residual value not exceeding 5% of original cost. In the year of purchase/sale, depreciation is pro-rated for the number of days the asset was actually in use during that financial year (1 Apr–31 Mar). This schedule is illustrative — always align the useful life and method with the company's board-approved depreciation policy.
